# Command line

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

Install with the Python package (`pip install red-xai-encrypt`), then:

```bash
redsecretsxai --help
python -m redsecretsxai --help          # same tool
python redsecrets.py --help             # source checkout only
```

Commands that take `-p` / `--password` prompt with no echo when you omit it. For a script, pass the password on stdin where the command reads a prompt (`printf '%s\n' "$PW" | redsecretsxai …`). Do not put secrets in shell history if you can avoid `-p`.

Press Ctrl-C during a folder or drive job to cancel. A cancelled job removes its temporary output.

Exit `0` on success. Usage errors exit `2`. Other failures exit `1` and print one line to stderr. Cancel exits `130`.

## Commands

| Command | What you use it for |
|---|---|
| `encode` / `decode` | Short message ↔ red-X PNG (password prompt) |
| `convert` | `.Red_SecretXAI` ↔ red-X PNG, without opening the file |
| `split` / `join` | One sealed blob across several red-X PNGs |
| `encrypt-file` / `decrypt-file` | One file, using a [port](Port-mode.md) |
| `encrypt-folder` / `decrypt-folder` | A folder, app, or project |
| `encrypt-drive` / `decrypt-drive` | A disk image or block device |
| `archive-preview` | List archive entries, write nothing |
| `init-port` | Create or unlock `.red-xai-port` |
| `hw-token` | Print this machine’s hardware token |
| `session` | Open and close a port session (check that the port unlocks) |

`encrypt-file` is not password mode. For a self-contained file, use the SDKs on [Seal and open](Seal-and-open.md), then [convert](Red-X-PNG.md).

## Red-X PNG

```bash
redsecretsxai convert report.Red_SecretXAI report.png
redsecretsxai convert report.png report-again.Red_SecretXAI --fmt bin
redsecretsxai encode -m "meet at 9" -o note.png
redsecretsxai decode -i note.png
redsecretsxai split --k 4 --n 6 --scheme 1 report.Red_SecretXAI parts/
redsecretsxai join joined.Red_SecretXAI parts/*.png
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `convert --fmt auto\|png\|bin` | Force the output. Default `auto` follows the destination name |
| `encode -m` / `-o` | Message and PNG path. `--module`, `--noise` optional |
| `decode -i` | PNG to read |
| `split --k K --n N` | Need K images, write N |
| `split --scheme 0\|1` | `1` (default) allows a missing image. `0` needs every image and `N` must equal `K` |

## Files (port)

```bash
redsecretsxai init-port --path /media/usb/.red-xai-port -y
redsecretsxai encrypt-file -i report.pdf --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
redsecretsxai decrypt-file -i report.pdf.Red_SecretXAI -o report.pdf --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-i` / `--input` | File to seal or open |
| `-o` / `--output` | Output path. Default for seal is `INPUT.Red_SecretXAI` |
| `-p` / `--password` | Password. Prompted when omitted |
| `--port` | `.red-xai-port` directory. Default `./.red-xai-port`. `RSX_PORT_PATH` is the same override |
| `--legacy-rsx1`, `--iters N` | Older self-contained file. Not the SDK password-mode API. Default iterations for that flag: 1,000,000 |

The port file used for these commands is `.red-xai-port/session.kxai`. `init-port` also prints a recovery key once. Save it offline. See [Recovery](Recovery.md).

## Folders

```bash
redsecretsxai encrypt-folder my-repo -o my-repo.Red_SecretXAI --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
redsecretsxai archive-preview my-repo.Red_SecretXAI --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
redsecretsxai decrypt-folder my-repo.Red_SecretXAI -d restored/ --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
redsecretsxai encrypt-folder my-repo -o my-repo.png --image
```

`--image` writes a red-X PNG (Python). `-q` / `--quiet` hides the progress bar. The password is prompted. It is not the `-p` flag on this command.

`archive-preview` prints one line per entry (`path`, type, size, mode) and a summary line starting with `#`.

## Drives

```bash
redsecretsxai encrypt-drive disk.img -o disk.Red_SecretXAI --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
redsecretsxai decrypt-drive disk.Red_SecretXAI -o disk-restored.img --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
sudo redsecretsxai encrypt-drive /dev/sdb -o usb-backup.Red_SecretXAI --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
redsecretsxai decrypt-drive usb-backup.Red_SecretXAI -o /dev/sdb --device --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
```

Reading a raw device usually needs administrator rights. `--device` asks you to type the destination path before it writes. Restore to an image file first when you can.

## Port and hardware

```bash
redsecretsxai init-port --path /media/usb/.red-xai-port -y
redsecretsxai hw-token
redsecretsxai session --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
```

`init-port` options: `--path`, `-p`, `-y` / `--yes` (accept the first-time prompt), `--iters`.

`hw-token` prints the token as hex on stdout, and the provider name plus a strength note on stderr. See [Hardware binding](Hardware-binding.md).

## Read-only decoder

If you built from source, `core/build/rsx-recover` opens a sealed file and does not update the port. Password on stdin:

```bash
printf '%s\n' "$PW" | rsx-recover --keymap .red-xai-port/session.kxai sealed.Red_SecretXAI restored.bin
```

Its exit codes: `0` ok, `1` usage, `2` wrong password or tampered data, `3` format or limits, `4` I/O or target exists, `5` other.

# FAQ

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

Usage and troubleshooting only. Product version 0.3.1.

**Where is the QR-code command?**  
There isn’t one. The delivery step is a red-X PNG: `redsecretsxai convert` for a sealed file, or `encode` / `decode` for a short message. Optional `split` and `join` spread one sealed file across several PNGs. See [Red-X PNG conversion](Red-X-PNG.md).

**What should I do first?**  
[Install](Install.md), [seal in password mode](Seal-and-open.md), then convert to a red-X PNG before you send it. Share the password on a different channel from the file.

**What can I seal?**  
Text (`RXAI2.` token or `encode`), one file, a folder, an app bundle, a zip or installer, a disk image, or a block device.

**Password mode or port mode?**  
Password mode: the file and the password are enough. Start there when you are sharing. Port mode: you also keep a `.red-xai-port` folder, ideally offline. Folders, drives, key cards, and hardware binding use the port. The CLI `encrypt-file` command uses a port. The SDK `mode="password"` / `Mode::Password` calls do not.

**I forgot the password.**  
A password-mode file cannot be opened without that password. For a port, rebuild from any *k* [key cards](Shamir-key-cards.md), or use the recovery key printed once by `init-port` or `create_port`. See [Recovery](Recovery.md).

**The other language won’t open my PNG.**  
JavaScript, C#, Java, and C++ read binary `.Red_SecretXAI` files in 0.3.1. Run `redsecretsxai convert image.png file.Red_SecretXAI --fmt bin`, then decrypt that file. Python `decrypt_file` reads the PNG form of an easy-API file directly. Helpers named `toImage` / `ToImage` / `to_image` on those SDKs throw until a later version and tell you to use Python.

**`decode` says to use `decrypt-file`.**  
That message (`PNG carries RSX3; use decrypt-file with --port`) means the PNG was made by `convert` from a CLI session file. Convert it back and open it with `decrypt-file` and the same port. `decode` is only for PNGs made by `encode`. Password-mode SDK files are opened with the SDK.

**Can I send a JPEG or a screenshot?**  
No. Keep the red-X PNG as a lossless file. A recompressed image or a photo of the screen is not a supported way to carry the sealed bytes.

**The command says the output already exists.**  
Pick a new path, move the old file, or pass overwrite on the SDK call. Decrypt will not replace an existing file unless you ask.

**Wrong password or the file was changed.**  
The password does not match, or the sealed bytes were edited. Port-mode files also need the same `.red-xai-port` you sealed with (`--port` / `port_path` / `portPath`).

**Setup was declined.**  
The first port-mode call asks before it creates `.red-xai-port`. Say yes, pass a callback that returns true, or use password mode. Declining does not delete your files.

**npm install failed on a script.**  
`npm install-scripts approve koffi`, then install again.

**Java will not start.**  
JDK 21 with `--enable-preview --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED`.

**Which machines have a prebuilt library?**  
Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64, and Windows x86_64. Elsewhere build `librsx` and set `RSX_LIB`. See [Install](Install.md). macOS and Windows arm64 are not in the 0.3.1 packages.

**Folder or drive job was cancelled.**  
Ctrl-C, or the SDK cancel signal, stops the job and removes temporary output. Run it again. Nothing half-written is left as the final file.

**Restore onto a disk says confirmation failed.**  
`decrypt-drive --device` asks you to type the device path. It must match `-o` exactly. Restore to an image file first when you can.

**`hw-token` printed a weak note.**  
The machine-id fallback is in use. The keymap can be tied to this computer, and that fallback does not add copy protection. Prefer a TPM, Keychain, or DPAPI provider when `hw_provider_name` reports one. See [Hardware binding](Hardware-binding.md).

**Can I list an archive without extracting?**  
Yes. `redsecretsxai archive-preview`, or `archive_preview` / `archivePreview` / `ArchivePreview` in the SDKs.

**Who do I contact?**  
Red-XAI LLC, support@infected-nation.com. Security reports go to that address as well. License: Apache-2.0.

# Folders, apps, and drives (optional)

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

These calls use [port mode](Port-mode.md). Create the port on first use with the setup callback or `init-port`. A macOS `.app` bundle is a folder. A zip, an installer, or one executable is a file: seal it with [password mode](Seal-and-open.md) or `encrypt-file`.

The archive keeps paths, permissions, and times. Extraction refuses absolute paths, `..` escapes, and unsafe links. Setuid bits are dropped unless you opt in with the flag below. The destination folder must exist (`decrypt_folder` creates it in the SDKs that say so; the CLI creates it too).

Ctrl-C on the CLI, or the cancel signal in an SDK, stops the job and removes temporary output. Existing outputs are not replaced.

To send a folder archive as a red-X PNG, seal it, then [convert](Red-X-PNG.md). Python can seal straight to a PNG with `output="image"` or `encrypt-folder --image`.

## Folders

```python
import os
from redxai import encrypt_folder, decrypt_folder

encrypt_folder(
    "photos", "pw-2026", "photos.Red_SecretXAI",
    port_path="/media/usb/.red-xai-port",
    on_setup_prompt=lambda: True,
)
os.makedirs("photos-restored", exist_ok=True)
decrypt_folder(
    "photos.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "photos-restored",
    port_path="/media/usb/.red-xai-port",
)
```

```js
const R = require('red-xai-encrypt');
const fs = require('fs');
R.encryptFolder('photos', 'pw-2026', 'photos.Red_SecretXAI', {
  portPath: '/media/usb/.red-xai-port',
  onSetupPrompt: () => true,
});
fs.mkdirSync('photos-restored', { recursive: true });
R.decryptFolder('photos.Red_SecretXAI', 'pw-2026', 'photos-restored', {
  portPath: '/media/usb/.red-xai-port',
});
```

```csharp
using RedXAI.Encrypt;
RedSecret.EncryptFolder("photos", "pw-2026", "photos.Red_SecretXAI",
    portPath: "/media/usb/.red-xai-port", onSetupPrompt: () => true);
Directory.CreateDirectory("photos-restored");
RedSecret.DecryptFolder("photos.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "photos-restored",
    portPath: "/media/usb/.red-xai-port");
```

```java
import com.redxai.encrypt.RedSecret;
RedSecret.encryptFolder("photos", "pw-2026", "photos.Red_SecretXAI",
    "port", "/media/usb/.red-xai-port", () -> true, RedSecret.ARCH_COMPRESS, null, null);
java.nio.file.Files.createDirectories(java.nio.file.Path.of("photos-restored"));
RedSecret.decryptFolder("photos.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "photos-restored",
    "/media/usb/.red-xai-port", null, 0, null, null);
```

```cpp
redxai::encrypt_folder("photos", "pw-2026", "photos.Red_SecretXAI",
    redxai::Mode::Port, "/media/usb/.red-xai-port", [] { return true; });
std::filesystem::create_directories("photos-restored");
redxai::decrypt_folder("photos.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "photos-restored",
    "/media/usb/.red-xai-port");
```

```bash
redsecretsxai encrypt-folder photos -o photos.Red_SecretXAI --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
redsecretsxai decrypt-folder photos.Red_SecretXAI -d photos-restored --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
```

C++ and Java reject folder seals that are not port mode. JavaScript folder calls always use the port.

### Apps

```python
from redxai import encrypt_folder, decrypt_folder
import os
encrypt_folder("MyApp.app", "pw-2026", "MyApp.Red_SecretXAI", on_setup_prompt=lambda: True)
os.makedirs("apps", exist_ok=True)
decrypt_folder("MyApp.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "apps")
```

Same call in the other languages: pass the `.app` directory (or any install folder) to `encryptFolder` / `EncryptFolder` / `encryptFolder` / `encrypt_folder`.

### Preview

List entries without writing files. CLI:

```bash
redsecretsxai archive-preview photos.Red_SecretXAI --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
```

```python
from redxai import _librsx as rsx
with rsx.session_open(b"pw-2026", ".red-xai-port/session.kxai") as s:
    entries, summary = rsx.archive_preview(s, "photos.Red_SecretXAI")
print(summary["files"], "files,", summary["total_bytes"], "bytes")
```

```js
const { entries, summary } = R.archivePreview('photos.Red_SecretXAI', 'pw-2026', {
  portPath: '/media/usb/.red-xai-port',
});
```

```csharp
var (entries, summary) = RedSecret.ArchivePreview("photos.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026",
    portPath: "/media/usb/.red-xai-port");
```

```java
var preview = RedSecret.archivePreview("photos.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "/media/usb/.red-xai-port");
```

### Progress and cancel

```python
import threading
from redxai import encrypt_folder, RedXAIError

stop = threading.Event()
try:
    encrypt_folder(
        "big", "pw-2026", "big.Red_SecretXAI",
        on_setup_prompt=lambda: True,
        progress=lambda done, total: print(f"\r{done:,} bytes", end=""),
        cancel=stop,
    )
except RedXAIError as e:
    print("stopped:", e)
```

JavaScript takes `progress(done, total)` and `signal` (an `AbortSignal`). C# takes `Action<ulong, ulong>` and a `CancellationToken`. Java takes `RedSecret.ProgressFn` and an `AtomicBoolean`. C++ takes a progress function and a `volatile int *` set to `1` to cancel.

`total` is `0` when the size is not known yet.

### Flags

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `1` | compress | Default for a new archive |
| `2` | allow symlinks | Extraction keeps links you opted into |
| `4` | allow setuid | Keep setuid bits |
| `8` | write device | Restore a drive onto a device. Also pass the device path as the confirmation name |

Python: `redxai._librsx.RSX_ARCH_COMPRESS` and the matching names. C++: `RSX_ARCH_COMPRESS`, `RSX_ARCH_ALLOW_SYMLINKS`, `RSX_ARCH_ALLOW_SETUID`, `RSX_ARCH_WRITE_DEVICE`. Java: `RedSecret.ARCH_*`. JavaScript documents the same numbers on `flags`.

## Drives and disk images

```python
from redxai import encrypt_drive, decrypt_drive
encrypt_drive("disk.img", "pw-2026", "disk.Red_SecretXAI", on_setup_prompt=lambda: True)
decrypt_drive("disk.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "disk-restored.img")
```

```js
const R = require('red-xai-encrypt');
R.encryptDrive('disk.img', 'pw-2026', 'disk.Red_SecretXAI', { onSetupPrompt: () => true });
R.decryptDrive('disk.Red_SecretXAI', 'pw-2026', 'disk-restored.img');
```

```csharp
RedSecret.EncryptDrive("disk.img", "pw-2026", "disk.Red_SecretXAI", onSetupPrompt: () => true);
RedSecret.DecryptDrive("disk.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "disk-restored.img");
```

```java
RedSecret.encryptDrive("disk.img", "pw-2026", "disk.Red_SecretXAI", null, () -> true,
    RedSecret.ARCH_COMPRESS, null, null);
RedSecret.decryptDrive("disk.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "disk-restored.img",
    null, null, 0, null, null, null);
```

```cpp
redxai::encrypt_drive("disk.img", "pw-2026", "disk.Red_SecretXAI");
redxai::decrypt_drive("disk.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "disk-restored.img");
```

`.img`, `.iso`, and `.dd` files work the same way. A block device such as `/dev/sdb` usually needs administrator rights.

Writing back onto a device requires the write-device flag and the destination path typed again as confirmation:

```bash
redsecretsxai decrypt-drive usb-backup.Red_SecretXAI -o /dev/sdb --device --port /media/usb/.red-xai-port
```

```python
from redxai import decrypt_drive
from redxai import _librsx as rsx
decrypt_drive(
    "usb-backup.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "/dev/sdb",
    flags=rsx.RSX_ARCH_WRITE_DEVICE,
    confirm_device_name="/dev/sdb",
)
```

```js
R.decryptDrive('usb-backup.Red_SecretXAI', 'pw-2026', '/dev/sdb', {
  flags: 8,
  confirmDeviceName: '/dev/sdb',
});
```

```csharp
RedSecret.DecryptDrive("usb-backup.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "/dev/sdb",
    flags: 8, confirmDeviceName: "/dev/sdb");
```

```java
RedSecret.decryptDrive("usb-backup.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "/dev/sdb",
    null, null, RedSecret.ARCH_WRITE_DEVICE, "/dev/sdb", null, null);
```

```cpp
redxai::decrypt_drive("usb-backup.Red_SecretXAI", "pw-2026", "/dev/sdb",
    "", nullptr, RSX_ARCH_WRITE_DEVICE, "/dev/sdb");
```

Restore to a new image file and check it before you write to a device.

# Red-SecretsXAI — how to use it

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

Seal a file with a password, then deliver it as a **red-X PNG**. That PNG step is the full-security delivery path (sometimes called QR-style conversion in product talk). There is no separate QR-code command. The real commands are `convert`, `encode`, `decode`, and optionally `split` and `join`.

Version **0.3.1** · Red-XAI LLC · support@infected-nation.com

## Recommended path

1. [Install](Install.md) the language you want. The command line ships with the Python package.
2. [Seal and open a file in password mode](Seal-and-open.md). The file plus the password is enough. Nothing else to set up.
3. [Turn the sealed file into a red-X PNG](Red-X-PNG.md) before you send it. Keep the PNG lossless (send the file itself, not a photo of the screen). Share the password on a different channel.

Python’s `encrypt_file` already writes a red-X PNG by default. JavaScript, C#, Java, and C++ write a binary `.Red_SecretXAI`. Run `convert` on that binary file so the copy you send is a red-X PNG.

## What you can seal

Text, a single file, a folder, an app bundle, a zip or installer, a disk image, or a whole drive. A file sealed in one language opens in the others when it is a binary `.Red_SecretXAI`. A red-X PNG opens in Python directly. Other languages open it after `convert` turns the PNG back into a `.Red_SecretXAI`.

## Two ways to keep the key

| | Password mode (start here) | Port mode (optional) |
|---|---|---|
| What you keep | The password | A `.red-xai-port` folder plus the password |
| Best for | Sharing one file or a short message | Day-to-day use on your own machine |
| Setup | None | Create the port on first use, ideally on a drive you keep offline |

Password mode is the path above. Port mode, folders, drives, decoys, key cards, hardware binding, and recovery are [optional steps](Port-mode.md) after that.

## Pages

- [Install](Install.md) — Python, JavaScript, C#, Java, C++, command line
- [Seal and open](Seal-and-open.md) — password mode
- [Red-X PNG conversion](Red-X-PNG.md) — recommended delivery step
- [Command line](CLI.md)
- [Python](Python.md) · [JavaScript](JavaScript.md) · [C#](CSharp.md) · [Java](Java.md) · [C++](Cpp.md)
- Optional: [Port mode](Port-mode.md) · [Folders, apps, and drives](Folders-apps-and-drives.md) · [Decoy passwords](Decoy-passwords.md) · [Shamir key cards](Shamir-key-cards.md) · [Hardware binding](Hardware-binding.md) · [Recovery](Recovery.md)

# Install

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

Red-SecretsXAI 0.3.1. Pick one language. You only need the others if you want them.

Prebuilt native libraries ship for **Linux x86_64**, **Linux aarch64**, and **Windows x86_64**. On any other platform, [build the native library](#build-the-native-library) and point the SDK at it.

## Python 3.10+

```bash
pip install red-xai-encrypt
```

This installs two import names: `redxai` (everyday calls) and `redsecretsxai` (red-X PNG tools, key cards, recovery, and the `redsecretsxai` command). The wheel also installs `numpy` and `Pillow`, which the image step uses.

## JavaScript (Node 18+)

```bash
npm install red-xai-encrypt
```

If npm blocks install scripts, approve the native loader once:

```bash
npm install-scripts approve koffi
```

## C# (.NET 8)

```bash
dotnet add package RedXAI.Encrypt
```

## Java (JDK 21)

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.redxai</groupId>
  <artifactId>red-xai-encrypt</artifactId>
  <version>0.3.1</version>
</dependency>
```

Compile and run with preview native access:

```bash
javac --release 21 --enable-preview YourApp.java
java --enable-preview --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED -cp red-xai-encrypt-0.3.1.jar:. YourApp
```

Gradle: `implementation("com.redxai:red-xai-encrypt:0.3.1")`.

## C++17

```cmake
find_package(red-xai-encrypt REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE RedXAI::red-xai-encrypt)
```

A vcpkg port is in `ports/red-xai-encrypt`. CMake 3.20 or newer. From a source checkout you can also compile against the headers and the library you built:

```bash
g++ -std=c++17 app.cpp -Ipackages/cpp/include -Lcore/build -lrsx -Wl,-rpath,core/build
```

## Command line

The CLI is part of the Python package. After `pip install red-xai-encrypt`:

```bash
redsecretsxai --help
python -m redsecretsxai --help
```

From a source checkout of this repository, the same tool is `python redsecrets.py --help`.

## Build the native library

Use this when a prebuilt library is not shipped for your machine, or when you want `RSX_LIB` to point at a library you built.

```bash
cmake -B core/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ -DRSX_SANITIZE=OFF -DRSX_SHARED=ON
cmake --build core/build
export RSX_LIB="$PWD/core/build/librsx.so"
```

That build also produces `core/build/rsx-recover`, the read-only recovery decoder. Every SDK honors `RSX_LIB`.

Next: [seal a file in password mode](Seal-and-open.md).

# Port mode (optional)

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

Use port mode when the key should live in a folder you keep, usually on a USB drive that stays offline, instead of traveling inside each file. Password mode is still the right default for a file you send to someone. See [Seal and open](Seal-and-open.md).

The folder name is `.red-xai-port`. The session file inside it is `session.kxai`. The first call can create it. Pass a setup callback that returns true, or answer the prompt. Declining the prompt seals nothing and deletes nothing.

## Create a port

```bash
redsecretsxai init-port --path /media/usb/.red-xai-port -y
```

`init-port` prints a recovery key once on stderr. Write it down offline. Details: [Recovery](Recovery.md).

## Python

```python
from redxai import encrypt_file, decrypt_file
import os

out = encrypt_file(
    "notes.txt", "pw-2026",
    mode="port",
    port_path="/media/usb/.red-xai-port",
    on_setup_prompt=lambda: True,
)
os.makedirs("restored", exist_ok=True)
print(decrypt_file(out, "pw-2026", out_dir="restored", port_path="/media/usb/.red-xai-port"))
```

`mode="port"` is the default. Opening detects the mode. If you pass `mode="password"` for a port file (or the reverse), the call tells you which mode the file actually uses.

## JavaScript

```js
const R = require('red-xai-encrypt');
const out = R.encryptFile('notes.txt', 'pw-2026', {
  mode: 'port',
  portPath: '/media/usb/.red-xai-port',
  onSetupPrompt: () => true,
});
R.decryptFile(out, 'pw-2026', { outDir: 'restored', portPath: '/media/usb/.red-xai-port' });
```

## C#

```csharp
using RedXAI.Encrypt;
var outPath = RedSecret.EncryptFile(
    "notes.txt", "pw-2026",
    mode: "port",
    portPath: "/media/usb/.red-xai-port",
    onSetupPrompt: () => true);
RedSecret.DecryptFile(outPath, "pw-2026", outDir: "restored", portPath: "/media/usb/.red-xai-port");
```

## Java

```java
import com.redxai.encrypt.RedSecret;
String out = RedSecret.encryptFile(
    "notes.txt", "pw-2026", "port", "/media/usb/.red-xai-port", () -> true, false);
RedSecret.decryptFile(out, "pw-2026", "restored", "port", "/media/usb/.red-xai-port", null, false);
```

`encryptFile(path, password)` with two arguments also uses port mode and may prompt.

## C++

```cpp
auto out = redxai::encrypt_file(
    "notes.txt", "pw-2026", redxai::Mode::Port,
    "/media/usb/.red-xai-port", [] { return true; });
redxai::decrypt_file(out, "pw-2026", "restored", "/media/usb/.red-xai-port");
```

An empty port path means `./.red-xai-port`.

## Change the port password

This rewraps the port. Sealed files stay as they are. Python, on an open session:

```python
from redxai import _librsx as rsx
with rsx.session_open(b"pw-2026", "/media/usb/.red-xai-port/session.kxai") as s:
    s.change_password("new-password")
```

The C API is `rsx_session_change_password`. The CLI has no password-change command in 0.3.1.

## What needs a port

[Folders, apps, and drives](Folders-apps-and-drives.md), [decoy passwords](Decoy-passwords.md) as a later packaging step, [Shamir key cards](Shamir-key-cards.md), [hardware binding](Hardware-binding.md), and [recovery](Recovery.md) all sit on top of a port or a sealed blob you already have. You can ignore them until you need them.

CLI file, folder, and drive commands take `--port`. See [Command line](CLI.md).

pages.markdown:
# Python

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

`pip install red-xai-encrypt` on Python 3.10+. Import `redxai` for everyday seal and open. Import `redsecretsxai` for red-X PNG tools, key cards, and recovery. Full steps: [Seal and open](Seal-and-open.md), [Red-X PNG](Red-X-PNG.md).

## Password mode

```python
from redxai import encrypt_file, decrypt_file, encrypt_text, decrypt_text
import os

os.makedirs("restored", exist_ok=True)
out = encrypt_file("notes.txt", "correct horse battery staple", mode="password")
# notes.txt.Red_SecretXAI is a red-X PNG. output="binary" writes the raw container.
print(decrypt_file(out, "correct horse battery staple", out_dir="restored"))

token = encrypt_text("hello", "correct horse battery staple", mode="password")
assert decrypt_text(token, "correct horse battery staple") == "hello"
```

## Red-X PNG

```python
from redsecretsxai.convert import to_image, to_binary, rerender
from redsecretsxai import encode_image, decode_image, capacity
from redsecretsxai.damage_recover import decode_robust

to_image("notes.txt.Red_SecretXAI", "notes.png")     # binary container only
to_binary("notes.png", "notes-again.Red_SecretXAI")
rerender("notes.png", "notes-v2.png", module=6)

png = encode_image(open("notes.txt.Red_SecretXAI", "rb").read(), path="wrapped.png")
blob = decode_image("wrapped.png")
plan = capacity.plan(len(blob))
print(plan.width, plan.height)
# decode_robust("scratched.png")  # damaged scan
```

CLI equivalents: `redsecretsxai convert`, `encode`, `decode`, `split`, `join`. See [Red-X PNG conversion](Red-X-PNG.md).

## Errors

```python
from redxai import decrypt_text, WrongPasswordError, NotRedSecretError, FileExistsRedXAIError, RedXAIError

try:
    decrypt_text(token, "wrong")
except WrongPasswordError:
    print("wrong password or the file was changed")
except NotRedSecretError:
    print("not a Red-SecretsXAI payload")
except FileExistsRedXAIError:
    print("output exists; pass overwrite=True")
except RedXAIError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e)
```

Also: `SetupDeclinedError`, `NoKeymapError`, `UnsafeFilenameError`, `NativeLibraryError`.

## Optional calls

| Call | Page |
|---|---|
| `encrypt_file(..., mode="port", port_path=, on_setup_prompt=)` | [Port mode](Port-mode.md) |
| `encrypt_folder` / `decrypt_folder` / `encrypt_drive` / `decrypt_drive` | [Folders, apps, and drives](Folders-apps-and-drives.md) |
| `redxai._librsx.duress_seal` / `duress_open` | [Decoy passwords](Decoy-passwords.md) |
| `redsecretsxai.keycards.split_port_key` / `restore_from_cards` | [Shamir key cards](Shamir-key-cards.md) |
| `redxai._librsx.session_create_hw` / `hw_token_ex` | [Hardware binding](Hardware-binding.md) |
| `create_port` / `unlock_port` | [Recovery](Recovery.md) |

A series of messages, opened in order, with the same 32-byte master and 16-byte salt on both sides:

```python
import os
from redxai import _librsx as rsx

master, salt = os.urandom(32), os.urandom(16)
with rsx.Ratchet.create(master, salt) as sender, rsx.Ratchet.create(master, salt) as receiver:
    frames = [sender.seal(f"frame {i}".encode()) for i in range(3)]
    print([receiver.open(f) for f in frames])
```

Share `master` and `salt` once, out of band. A replayed or skipped frame is rejected.

## Easy API

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `encrypt_text(text, password, *, mode="port", port_path=None, on_setup_prompt=None)` | Returns an `RXAI2.` line |
| `decrypt_text(blob, password, *, mode=None, port_path=None, on_setup_prompt=None)` | |
| `encrypt_file(path, password, *, mode="port", output="image", port_path=None, on_setup_prompt=None, overwrite=False)` | `output` is `"image"` or `"binary"` |
| `decrypt_file(path, password, *, out_dir=None, mode=None, port_path=None, on_setup_prompt=None, overwrite=False)` | Restores the original file name inside `out_dir` |
| `encrypt_folder(src, password, out_path, *, mode="port", port_path=None, on_setup_prompt=None, flags=1, progress=None, cancel=None, output="binary")` | `output="image"` wraps a PNG |
| `decrypt_folder(archive, password, dest_dir, *, port_path=None, on_setup_prompt=None, flags=0, progress=None, cancel=None)` | |
| `encrypt_drive(...)` / `decrypt_drive(..., confirm_device_name=None)` | Device writes need `flags` write-device and `confirm_device_name` |

`FILE_EXT` is `.Red_SecretXAI`. `TEXT_PREFIX` is `RXAI2.`.

pages.markdown:
# Recovery (optional)

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

Use this after you have a [port](Port-mode.md), or when a sealed file will not open and you still have a backup of the port. Password mode files have no separate recovery key: the password is the only opener. Put a copy of the red-X PNG or the `.Red_SecretXAI` somewhere safe, and keep the password elsewhere.

## Recovery key from `init-port`

```bash
redsecretsxai init-port --path /media/usb/.red-xai-port -y
```

The command prints `Recovery key (hex)` once, on stderr. It is not shown again. Store it offline. The Python create path does the same with a callback:

```python
from redsecretsxai import create_port, unlock_port

info = create_port(
    "/media/usb/.red-xai-port",
    b"pw-2026",
    on_backup_prompt=lambda hex_key: open("RECOVERY-KEY.txt", "w").write(hex_key + "\n"),
)
# info["recovery_hex"] is the same key, shown this once.
# Do not pass recovery_key= into create_port. The key is generated for you.

master = unlock_port("/media/usb/.red-xai-port", recovery_key=open("RECOVERY-KEY.txt").read().strip())
```

`unlock_port` takes the hex string or the raw bytes. The password form is `unlock_port(path, password=b"pw-2026")` and returns the 32-byte master key. That unlocks the classic port files. It does not by itself open a `.Red_SecretXAI`. To open files, use the session (below) or your usual decrypt call once the port is intact.

`tripwire_enabled=True` on `create_port` is optional. After repeated failed password attempts, the password unlock is erased. The recovery key still unlocks. Too many wrong recovery keys raise `RecoveryBackoff` and you wait before trying again.

JavaScript `createPort` / `unlockPort`, C# `CreatePort` / `UnlockPort`, and Java `createPort` / `unlockPortWithRecoveryKey` throw `available in the Python SDK only … until v0.4`. Use Python or `init-port`.

## Key cards

Any *k* [Shamir cards](Shamir-key-cards.md) rebuild `session.kxai` under a new password. Use that when the port folder is lost and the cards are not.

## Read-only open

A read-only session does not write the port. Python:

```python
from redxai import _librsx as rsx
ro, warnings = rsx.session_open_readonly(b"pw-2026", ".red-xai-port/session.kxai")
# rsx.open_(ro, sealed_bytes) or rsx.decrypt_file(ro, ...)
ro.close()
```

From a source build, the `rsx-recover` tool is read-only as well. Password on stdin. See [Command line](CLI.md).

## Keymap backup

On an open C session you can write a backup under a second password and restore it later. Python binding surface is the C API (`rsx_keymap_backup`, `rsx_keymap_verify_backup`, `rsx_keymap_restore`). C++ example:

```cpp
const std::string bpw = "backup-password";
rsx_keymap_backup(session, reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t *>(bpw.data()), bpw.size(),
                  "session.backup.kxai");
```

Restore:

```cpp
const std::string npw = "new-password";
rsx_keymap_restore(
    reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t *>(bpw.data()), bpw.size(), "session.backup.kxai",
    reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t *>(npw.data()), npw.size(),
    ".red-xai-port/session.kxai");
```

There is no CLI backup command in 0.3.1.

## Damaged red-X PNG

`convert` and `decode_image` already tolerate a modest amount of damage. For a scratched or skewed scan, use `decode_robust` as shown on [Red-X PNG conversion](Red-X-PNG.md), then open the sealed bytes with the password or the port.

pages.title: Red-X PNG conversion (full-security delivery)
pages.markdown:
# Red-X PNG conversion (full-security delivery)

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

Do this after you [seal](Seal-and-open.md). The sealed payload stays sealed. Converting to a red-X PNG does not ask for the password and does not open the file. Send the PNG as a file so it stays lossless. Share the password somewhere else.

People sometimes call this step QR-style conversion. The product command is **`convert`** (and `encode` / `decode` for a short message). There is no `qr` command and no separate QR library to install.

Python’s password-mode `encrypt_file` already writes a red-X PNG named `something.Red_SecretXAI`. You can send that file as-is. Use `convert` when the sealed file is a binary container (the other SDKs, Python `output="binary"`, or the CLI `encrypt-file` / folder / drive commands).

The image tools below are the Python package and the `redsecretsxai` command. In JavaScript, C#, Java, and C++ the same-looking helpers (`toImage`, `ToImage`, `to_image`, `splitImages`, …) throw `available in the Python SDK only … until v0.4`. Call the CLI.

## 1. Binary container to red-X PNG

```bash
redsecretsxai convert notes.txt.Red_SecretXAI notes.png
```

Turn the PNG back into a container before a non-Python SDK or the CLI opens it:

```bash
redsecretsxai convert notes.png notes-again.Red_SecretXAI --fmt bin
```

If you sealed with an SDK in password mode, open `notes-again.Red_SecretXAI` with that SDK and the same password. If you sealed with the CLI (`encrypt-file`, `encrypt-folder`, or `encrypt-drive`), open it with the matching command and the same `--port`. `convert` does not change which of those you need.

Python can do the same calls without the shell:

```python
from redsecretsxai.convert import convert, to_image, to_binary

to_image("notes.txt.Red_SecretXAI", "notes.png")
to_binary("notes.png", "notes-again.Red_SecretXAI")
# or one function; fmt is "auto", "png", or "binary" ("bin" is accepted)
convert("notes.txt.Red_SecretXAI", "notes.png", fmt="png")
convert("notes.png", "notes-again.Red_SecretXAI", fmt="bin")
```

`fmt="auto"` uses the destination extension. `.png` becomes a red-X PNG. `.Red_SecretXAI` becomes the binary container.

Give the PNG a new look later without the password:

```python
from redsecretsxai.convert import rerender
rerender("notes.png", "notes-v2.png", module=6)
```

`module` is the pixel size of each cell (default 5). `noise` changes the texture (default 30). Optional appearance flags you can pass: `chromatic`, `pyramid`, `operators`.

Check the image size before you encode a large payload:

```python
from redsecretsxai import capacity
p = capacity.plan(20_000)
print(p.width, "x", p.height)
```

## 2. Short message straight into a PNG

`encode` asks for a password and writes a red-X PNG. `decode` reads it back. This is the message path, separate from `encrypt_file`.

```bash
redsecretsxai encode -m "meet at 9" -o note.png
redsecretsxai decode -i note.png
```

Add `-p` only in a context where the password will not be saved in shell history. Otherwise let the command prompt. Optional: `--module` and `--noise`.

`decode` only opens a PNG written by `encode`. If it prints `PNG carries RSX3; use decrypt-file with --port (session), not decode`, that image was made by `convert` from a CLI session file. Convert it back and open it with `decrypt-file` and the [port](Port-mode.md). A password-mode SDK file is opened with the SDK (Python can open the PNG directly; the other languages need `convert --fmt bin` first).

## 3. Python opens the PNG directly

When Python wrote the file (`encrypt_file`, including the default image output), or you only renamed that PNG:

```python
from redxai import decrypt_file
import os
os.makedirs("restored", exist_ok=True)
print(decrypt_file("notes.txt.Red_SecretXAI", "correct horse battery staple", out_dir="restored"))
```

`decrypt_file` accepts that PNG. It also accepts a PNG made by `convert` from a password-mode `.Red_SecretXAI` written by any of the SDKs. JavaScript, C#, Java, and C++ do not read the PNG in 0.3.1. Convert to `.Red_SecretXAI` first, then call `decryptFile` / `DecryptFile` / `decryptFile` / `decrypt_file` on the binary. A file sealed by the CLI is opened with the CLI and its port, not with `decrypt_file`.

## 4. Optional: several PNGs (`split` / `join`)

Spread one sealed container across images. `--scheme 1` (the default) can rebuild with a missing piece. `--scheme 0` needs every piece, and `--n` must equal `--k`.

```bash
redsecretsxai split --k 4 --n 6 --scheme 1 notes.txt.Red_SecretXAI parts/
redsecretsxai join joined.Red_SecretXAI parts/*.png
```

With `--k 4 --n 6 --scheme 1`, join still works when one of the six PNGs is missing. Do not count on joining if more than one is missing. Then open `joined.Red_SecretXAI` with the original password.

Python:

```python
from redsecretsxai import fountain_encode as fc

blob = open("notes.txt.Red_SecretXAI", "rb").read()
pngs = fc.encode_chunks(blob, 4, 6, fc.SCHEME_FOUNTAIN)  # scheme 1
fc.write_package("parts", pngs)                          # parts/part_0000.png …
parts = fc.read_package("parts")
open("joined.Red_SecretXAI", "wb").write(fc.decode_and_reassemble(parts[1:]))
```

`SCHEME_SPLIT` is scheme 0. Limits: `1 <= k <= n`, `k <= 2048`, and `k * n <= 4194304`. A very small sealed file needs a small `k`.

Folder archives can be wrapped in one step from Python or the CLI:

```bash
redsecretsxai init-port -y
redsecretsxai encrypt-folder photos -o photos.png --image
```

```python
from redxai import encrypt_folder
encrypt_folder("photos", "pw", "photos.png", on_setup_prompt=lambda: True, output="image")
```

`--image` / `output="image"` on a folder uses a port. See [Folders, apps, and drives](Folders-apps-and-drives.md).

## 5. If the PNG was damaged

Keep a binary `.Red_SecretXAI` (or a `split` set with a spare image) as the copy you store. For a PNG that was scratched, cropped a little, rotated, or mildly skewed:

```python
from redsecretsxai import decode_image
from redsecretsxai.damage_recover import decode_robust

blob = decode_image("notes.png")       # first try
# blob = decode_robust("notes.png")    # scratched, skewed, or blurry scan
open("notes-again.Red_SecretXAI", "wb").write(blob)
```

`decode_image` and `decode_robust` return the sealed bytes. They do not need the password. Open the result with the SDK or with `decrypt-file`.

Send PNG files as attachments or file copies. A JPEG, a messenger recompress, or a photo of the screen is not a supported carrier.

Next, only if you need them: [port mode](Port-mode.md) and the other optional pages linked from [Home](Home.md).

Security testing and reporting
pages.markdown:
# Security testing and reporting

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

Red-SecretsXAI is pre-audit. Publication of these usage guides is not a security certification or a guarantee of cryptographic strength.

## Scope

Use dummy data and files you own in an isolated local test environment. Do not test live Red-XAI infrastructure, third-party services, other people's devices, or other people's data under this invitation.

## Report privately

Email **support@infected-nation.com** with the subject **SECURITY: Red-SecretsXAI**. Do not post vulnerability details or real secrets in public issues.

Include the package and version, operating system, encryption mode and settings, exact reproduction steps, expected and actual results, and any dummy-data proof of concept. State whether you had the password, port, keymap, recovery key, or key cards, and what information you recovered without them.

Never send real passwords, private keys, production data, or someone else's information. Use disposable test credentials in any reproduction.

This documentation publication does not announce a paid bounty.

pages.title: Shamir key cards (optional)
pages.markdown:
# Shamir key cards (optional)

> **Public documentation only.** The implementation repository remains private. These guides describe the wiki's 0.3.1 interface; published package versions and platform support may differ. Source-checkout/build steps require separately authorized source access. Examples use dummy credentials.

After you have a [port](Port-mode.md), you can split its key into *n* red-X card images. Any *k* of them rebuild the port under a new password. Keep the cards in different places. Fewer than *k* cards are not enough to rebuild.

In 0.3.1 the card files are a Python tool. JavaScript `splitPortKey`, C# `SplitPortKey`, Java `splitPortKey`, and C++ `split_port_key` throw `available in the Python SDK only … until v0.4`.

You need `2 <= k <= n <= 255`.

## Make the cards

The port must already unlock with this password. The session file is `session.kxai` inside the port folder.

```python
from redsecretsxai import keycards

cards = keycards.split_port_key(
    b"pw-2026",
    "/media/usb/.red-xai-port/session.kxai",
    3, 5,
    "cards",
)
print(cards[0])   # cards/red-x-keycard-1-of-5-k3.png
```

That writes five PNGs. Any three rebuild the key. Print them or copy them to separate storage. They are not a substitute for the [recovery key](Recovery.md) unless you have chosen to rely on the cards.

## Rebuild a port from cards

```python
import os
from redsecretsxai import keycards
from redxai import _librsx as rsx

os.makedirs("new-port", exist_ok=True)
keycards.restore_from_cards(
    cards[:3],
    b"new-password",
    "new-port/session.kxai",
)
with rsx.session_open(b"new-password", "new-port/session.kxai") as s:
    print("port rebuilt", s.path)
```

`cards` can be paths or PNG bytes. `keycards.read_card(path)` reads one card back to its share bytes if you need to inspect a single file before you combine.

A wrong mix (cards from different splits, or too few) fails the combine. It does not write a usable port.

Sealed files do not change. Open them with the new port and the new password.
